data.body:
# Phase 1 EXIT — confirmed root cause (rebar-debug)

Two causes, and two are needed: one explains the **growth rate**, the other explains the
**failure to reclaim**. Neither alone explains both symptoms.

---

## RC-A (why there was so much to reclaim) — every review writes a full ~620 MiB / ~70,000-file copy of the ticket store, keyed on a ref that advances every ~26 seconds, and nothing ever frees it

`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:99` calls `materialize_tickets(...)` on every attested gate
resolution. `materialize_tickets` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:675-703`)
content-addresses the entry as `<store>/tickets-<sha>` and builds it via `_materialize_tree`
(`:373-410`, `git read-tree` + `git checkout-index`) — every file written fresh, no
hardlinking, no delta, no per-review release (`SnapshotHandle._cleanup` at `:199` is never
assigned by any producer). `_pin_tickets_sha` (`:534-609`) pins the **live** tracker HEAD via
`config.tracker_dir()`, and `tracker_dir_override()` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:65-79`)
returns the container's `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` verbatim, so the key is the tickets branch tip.

Measured independently on this checkout:

- tickets tree = **69,984 blobs** (≈620 MiB; ~800 MiB allocated). Code snapshot for comparison:
  41.6 MiB / 3,131 files — **15× smaller**.
- **1,374 commits** on `origin/tickets` in the 10-hour incident window — HEAD moves every ~26 s.
- each of the last 5 consecutive tickets commits changed **exactly 1 file**.

So a ~1-file delta produces a fresh 620 MiB copy: ~10^5× write amplification, on a key with
effectively **zero reuse**. At ~0.85 GiB per review (tickets + code entry) and the observed
review cadence this models **2.5-10 GiB/h**; measured growth was **4.4 GiB/h**. Match.

The review-bot's own `code_review` artifact write (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`,
`docker-compose.yml:120`) guarantees the ref advances between reviews even if nothing else in
the fleet were writing.

## RC-B (why nothing reclaimed it before the alarm) — both janitor eviction triggers are structurally unreachable in this deployment, and the third one the ADR promises was never implemented

`_gc_pass` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:303-345`) has exactly two eviction predicates:

- **`need_space = free < cfg.free_watermark_bytes`** (`janitor.py:318`), default **2 GiB**
  (`janitor.py:53`). That is an **absolute** floor and it is disk-size-blind. On a 30-GiB root
  it is crossed only at **93.3% used** — above the `rebar-root-disk-pressure` threshold of
  **85%** (`infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:226`) and above the observed **90%** peak.
- **`too_cold = mtime < now - max_age_seconds`**, default **7 days** (`janitor.py:55`). The
  store lives on a writable layer destroyed on every redeploy — 23 reclaim events in 4 days,
  i.e. a container lifetime of hours. **No entry can ever reach 7 days**; the cold-trim is dead
  code here.
- The third trigger, promised by `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:72-73` and by
  the module's own contract docstring (`janitor.py:13-15`) — "backstopped by the
  incrementally-maintained byte total" — **does not exist**: `_gc_pass` reads only `free` and
  `mtime`. The only reader of `byte_total` is `startup_sweep` (`janitor.py:251`), for
  reconciliation. There is no store-size cap knob at all (`docs/config.md:474-484`).
- Compounding it: `materialize_tickets` bypasses `cache.acquire` and so **never calls
  `add_bytes`** — even if the ADR's backstop existed it would under-count the dominant consumer
  to **zero**.

The janitor **is** started (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:134-136`) and ran every 300 s
throughout the incident. It correctly evicted nothing. "GC never ran" is falsified.

---

## Proof — discriminating experiments

**E1 (runtime, decisive for RC-B).** Drove the real `rebar._snapshot.janitor.run_gc()` with
injected free-space values for a 30-GiB root against 5 warm, out-of-grace, not-cold entries:

| root used | free injected | evicted |
|---|---|---|
| 80% (`DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`) | 6.00 GiB | **0** |
| **85% (CloudWatch ALARM floor)** | 4.50 GiB | **0** |
| **90% (observed incident peak)** | 3.00 GiB | **0** |
| 94% (past the watermark) | 1.80 GiB | 5 |

Provably inert across the entire range the incident occupied. A `dynamic` claim confirmed by
execution, not by reading the constant.

**E5 (falsifies the Docker-cache rival).** Buildkit cache and image layers cannot exist without
a build, and autodeploy only builds when `main` advances with a `BOT_PATHS`/`SECRETS_PATHS`
change. Cutting the `root_disk_used_percent` series at every such commit (+15 min for
build/prune, excluding intervals containing a reclaim) yields 12 maximal build-free intervals:
**10 of 12 grew faster than 0.5 GiB/h; median +1.12, max +3.93 GiB/h — with no rebuild
possible.** The single non-growing interval (+0.00) is the one where *review* activity nearly
stopped (0.6M LLM tokens). Growth tracks reviews, not builds. **Ticket hypothesis 2 (Docker
prune timing) is rejected.**

Three further nails in that rival: (i) the largest reclaim, **12.6 GiB**, exceeds the entire
5 GB buildkit ceiling plus any plausible dangling-image set; (ii) `--keep-storage` leaves a
*variable* LRU residue, so 23 independent prunes cannot converge on an identical floor, whereas
destroying a container writable layer converges **by construction** — and 23 of 23 drops land
on **48%**; (iii) with `deploy_deferrals = 0` for every bucket 20:30-21:50, the `TARGET ==
DEPLOYED` no-op branch *was* being taken, so from 21:25 (80%) a pressure prune fired roughly
every 10 min — and the disk climbed **80% → 90% straight through them**.

**E3.** All 23 reclaim events over 2026-08-15→19 are preceded by a `BOT_PATHS` commit (22/23
within 60 min); no reclaim occurs in any build-free window. Reclamation is tied to container
recreation, never to the pressure gate.

**E4.** `deploy_deferrals` was 0 through 21:50; the disk crossed 80% at 21:25 and 85% at 21:35,
**20-30 min before the first deferral**. The drain gate is a bystander that delayed the
recreation which would otherwise have reset the disk sooner — an aggravating factor, not the
cause. `deploy_errors` = `voter_errors` = `review_interrupts` = 0 throughout.

**E2.** With `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` unset, `store_root()` resolves under `tempfile.gettempdir()`.
`REBAR_GATE_*` appears **nowhere** in `docker-compose.yml`, `Dockerfile.reviewbot`, or
`fetch-secrets.sh`, and the `review-bot` service's only mounts are `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot`
and `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` (bind-backed onto the separate 50-GiB EBS volume) plus
a read-only key file — no `tmpfs`. So `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` is on the container's
**writable layer**, on the 30-GiB root.

**Ruled out as the leak:** the per-change clone workdir
(`src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:572`, `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` in a `with` block —
released on every exit path); the LLM-workflow run snapshot (`llm/workflow/snapshot.py:70-74`,
rooted at that temp clone and capped at 512 MiB, `:43`); journald (survives container
recreation, so it cannot produce a constant floor).

---

## Every symptom accounted for

| symptom | cause |
|---|---|
| root disk 71% → 90% in ~1 h at 4.4 GiB/h | RC-A: ~0.85 GiB of fresh snapshot per review |
| the alarm breached 85% and kept climbing | RC-B: the only bounding mechanism cannot engage until 93.3% |
| abrupt 90% → **48%** at 22:05 | deploy recreated the container; the writable layer (store included) destroyed |
| **all 23** drops land on the identical 48% | wholesale destruction of an ephemeral layer, not a variable-residue prune |
| `reviewbot_healthy` = 0 in the 22:05 bucket only | the 5-min host probe sampled during that recreation; 1-of-23 is the expected hit rate for a seconds-long window |
| `voter_errors` = 0 | never reached ENOSPC — recreation came before exhaustion |
| `deploy_deferrals` 2/3/1 at 21:55-22:05 | the drain gate delayed the recreation, so this episode reached 90% instead of resetting earlier |
| story 28f9's mitigation did not prevent it | `prune_docker_caches` cannot reclaim a **running** container's writable layer, whenever it fires |

No residual symptom is unexplained.

---

## Defect legitimacy

**RC-B — `defect` / `incomplete-implementation`.** Cited authorities, all violated:

- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:500-508` — the documented defense ordering: the janitor
  "reclaims `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` on a free-space watermark", and the alarm pages "so
  exhaustion is caught **before** it silently fail-closes the gate." In practice the ordering is
  inverted: the backstop fires and the primary never does.
- `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:72-73` and `janitor.py:13-15` — both specify a
  byte-total backstop that `_gc_pass` does not implement (`incomplete-implementation`).
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:209-215, 226` — the alarm contract names 85% as the
  actionable threshold and `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` as a reclaim target for it.
- Prior **closed** bug `7a41-95f4-c38c-4b5a` AC2 — "a disk-headroom check … so exhaustion is
  caught **before** it vetoes reviews." A previously-fixed behaviour class.
- This ticket's own AC4.

Not `environment-or-config`: an operator *can* set `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_BYTES`, but the
shipped **default** is what is wrong, and an absolute byte floor is disk-size-blind by
construction — no single absolute value is correct across hosts.

**RC-A — `defect`.** `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md` D2 rests on "an immutable
SHA is a perfect cache key", which holds only for keys with **reuse**. The tickets ref has
none — it advances every ~26 s — so the structure is not a cache but an append-only log of
620-MiB full copies, contradicting the ADR's own claim that the store is bounded and
reclaimable.

---

## What was NOT established

`ssm:SendCommand` is blocked in this session, so there is **no** host `du` / `docker system df`
/ journald evidence in this record. RC-A's dominance rests on measured artifact sizes, measured
ref churn, the code path, and the rate match — not on a direct measurement of the live
directory. The one host operation still wanted, purely read-only:
`docker ps --size` and `du -xh --max-depth=1 /tmp` inside `compose-review-bot-1`. It would
confirm the split rather than change the conclusion.

Phase 1 complete. Siblings filed for the two causes that are out of this ticket's repair scope.
